claims.original_statement: Totalization and fixed-factor tensor totalization are exact when the target additive category has countable direct sums.
claims.proved_statement: For either outer-complex convention, double complexes whose diagonal coproducts exist form a full triangulated subcategory, and Tot on it is exact with the original comparison. Fixed-factor tensor functors are exact on their corresponding domains; same-side bounded factors require only finite biproducts.
claims.hypotheses: Additive categories, original commuting double-complex differentials, the specified diagonal coproducts, and bilinearity for tensor products. No strict-fullness or automatic existence from homotopy equivalence is asserted.
claims.propagation: Exact component comparisons checked; existing tensor source conclusions unchanged.

claims.original_statement: A sequence of chain maps with the listed staggered cohomology vanishings factors through a lower truncation; dual assertion included.
claims.proved_statement: The factorization holds for arbitrary derived morphisms with any integer initial cutoff b and target cutoff b-n. If final cohomology vanishes below a and n>b-a, the composite is zero. The ideal of cohomologically zero endomorphisms of an object of amplitude [a,b] has power b-a+1 equal to zero, with the complete finite inverse for 1-u.
claims.hypotheses: Abelian category; source upper bound, the exact staggered vanishing maps, and final lower bound only for zero composition. No intermediate boundedness or homological-dimension hypothesis.
claims.propagation: All five direct uses checked for this implication. More Algebra target repaired; existing constants retained, and c(t+1) supplies the local annihilation step.
